incumbent.name: Heath VanNatter
incumbent.summary: Heath VanNatter, a Kokomo Republican and homebuilder, has represented House District 38 since 2010 {caucus_vannatter}. He chairs the House Employment, Labor and Pensions Committee and also serves on the Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development and Public Policy committees {caucus_vannatter}.
record: Committees: Employment, Labor and Pensions (chair); Commerce, Small Business and Economic Development; Public Policy. 2026 interim: chair of the Interim Study Committee on Employment and Labor and member of the Pension Management Oversight committee {caucus_vannatter} {caucus_interim_2026}.

Jan. 2025: Authored HB 1630, which would have legalized marijuana for adults 21 and older and created a Cannabis Commission; it was referred to the Courts and Criminal Code Committee and received no further action {fd_hb1630} {wndu_hb1630}.

April 10, 2025: Voted yes when the House passed SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law, 65-29 {rc_sea1_433}. April 25, 2025: Voted yes on the 2025 state budget conference report (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 {rc_hb1001_576}.
Dec. 5, 2025: Voted yes on HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41 {rc_hb1032_28}; the Senate rejected it 31-19 on Dec. 11 {wndu_senate_rejects}.

2026 session: House sponsor of SEA 185, which targets foreign-made vaping products with harmful chemicals and tightens tobacco and e-cigarette permit and age-verification rules {caucus_sea185}. Co-authored HEA 1145, which provides a one-time extra payment to retired public employees by Oct. 1, 2026 {caucus_hea1145}.

race_context: House District 38 includes all of Carroll and Tipton counties and parts of Cass, Clinton, Howard and Tippecanoe counties, per the House Republican caucus {caucus_vannatter}; the Pharos-Tribune describes it as including the west side of Kokomo and southern Cass County {pharos_spotlight}.

May 5, 2026 primaries: VanNatter won the Republican nomination with 4,676 votes (58.5%) to 3,316 (41.5%) for Mark Hufford; Nate Stout was unopposed for the Democratic nomination {wiki_2026}. In Howard County, VanNatter received 1,432 votes to Hufford's 733 {howard_results}.

Key differences: Stout emphasizes public school funding, rural health care and Medicaid, and opposes prioritizing private-school vouchers {br_stout} {kt_stout}; VanNatter voted for the 2025 budget, property-tax law and redistricting bill {rc_hb1001_576} {rc_sea1_433} {rc_hb1032_28} and has authored a bill to legalize adult-use marijuana {fd_hb1630}.
The Cass County Democrats hosted a candidate spotlight with Stout in Logansport in August 2026 {pharos_spotlight}. No debate between the candidates was found.

candidates.summary: Heath VanNatter is the Republican incumbent, first elected in 2010, and chairs the House Employment, Labor and Pensions Committee {caucus_vannatter}. He won a contested Republican primary in May 2026 {wiki_2026}.
background: Owner of VanNatter Construction and a small business owner for more than 20 years; past president of the Howard County Home Builders Association; director of the Indiana Builders Association and the National Association of Home Builders; former Howard County Plan Commission member; Northwestern High School graduate; lives in Howard County {caucus_vannatter}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over Mark Hufford, 58.5% to 41.5% {wiki_2026}.

items: The caucus says he emphasizes economic development, job retention, fiscal responsibility and affordable housing {caucus_vannatter}.
Said of SEA 185: "This new law is about drawing a clear line to protect Hoosiers and prevent dangerous products from reaching consumers" {caucus_sea185}.
Said the extra retiree payment in HEA 1145 "ensures their fixed incomes can better keep pace with rising costs" {caucus_hea1145}.
On HB 1630 (2025), said "It's time for Indiana to join our neighbors and most of the rest of the country in legalizing marijuana" {fox59_hb1630}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No statements by VanNatter about Stout were found.
plans: Said interim study committee work would support workers while being responsible with taxpayer dollars: "Thoughtful data-driven policymaking will ensure we continue supporting workers" {caucus_interim_2026}.
endorsements_finance: No 2026 endorsements or fundraising figures were found.
gaps: Search snippets described a Journal & Courier primary Q&A in which Hufford cited concerns over land and water use for solar, wind and data projects and opposed marijuana legalization, and VanNatter named jobs and the economy as his top issue; the article (and a reprint) returned 403 and was not read.
That snippet also described the district as reaching Monticello, which is not in the counties the caucus lists; unverified.

candidates.summary: Nate Stout, a Tipton native and business consultant, is the Democratic nominee {kt_stout} {br_stout}. He emphasizes public schools, rural health care and local economies {kt_stout}.
background: Owner and founder of Stout Consulting Group since 2025; previously in sales management at Séura, Johnson Outdoors and Callaway Golf; bachelor's degree in marketing from Indiana University Bloomington {br_stout}.
path_to_ballot: Announced in February 2026 {kt_stout}; unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wiki_2026} {howard_results}.

items: Wants to "Raise teacher pay and restore respect for the teaching profession" and "Fully fund our public schools first," with private and voucher programs not taking priority {br_stout}.
Wants to "Protect our Medicaid program," keep rural hospitals and clinics open and staffed, and expand maternal and neonatal care in rural counties {br_stout}.
Supports small-town grocery and local service businesses, main street renewal, and working with local leaders on grants and infrastructure such as broadband and roads {br_stout}.
Says he wants to hold government accountable for its spending and that the election will decide "whether resources continue to be siphoned away from rural communities" {kt_stout}.

on_incumbent: No direct statements about VanNatter were found {kt_stout}.
plans: Presents his platform as practical rather than party-line, focused on education, rural health care and local economies {kt_stout}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were found.
gaps: His campaign site (hoosierstoelectnatestout.com) redirected to a placeholder page or returned errors on Oct. 10, 2026; policy text was read via BallotReady.
Little news coverage beyond his February 2026 announcement and an August 2026 Cass County Democrats event.
